title: CWP/22153/2021 of KARAM SINGH Vs STATE OF PUNJAB AND OTHERS
judge: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HARPREET SINGH BRAR
text:
1 IN THE HIGH COURT OF PUNJAB AND HARYANA AT CHANDIGARH 253 CWP-22153-2021 Date of Decision: August 12, 2025 Karam Singh .....Petitioner VERSUS State of Punjab and others .....Respondents CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HARPREET SINGH BRAR Present : Ms. Geetanjali and Ms. Muskan, Advocates for the petitioner. Ms. Arundhati Kulshreshtha, AAG, Punjab-State. Mr. Manjot Gujral with Mr. Maninderpreet Singh, Advocates for respondent No.7. Mr. Aditya Pratap Duggal, Advocate for respondent No.8 HARPREET SINGH BRAR, J. (Oral)

1. The present writ petition has been filed under Article 226/227 of the Constitution of India with a prayer for issuance of an appropriate writ, order or directions especially in the nature of certiorari for quashing the impugned order dated 16.07.2021(Annexure P-13) passed by respondent No.4 and the impugned order dated 28.07.2021 (Annexure P-14) passed by respondent No.2 in violation of Punjab Civil Services Rules and further for issuance of a direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to grant No Objection Certificate (NOC) and to release the complete pensionary benefits.

2. Learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 3-State has referred to the reply filed on behalf of respondents No.1 to 3 and submits that the disciplinary action has been initiated in terms of the Punjab Civil Services Rule 2.2 of Volume 2 Chapter 2 and the department has in fact released the 2 pension to the petitioner and only gratuity has been only withheld. The same has been done in the light of the Punjab Civil Services Rules Volume 2 Rule 9.14 C, which empowers the competent authority to withtheld the gratuity until the final conclusion of the departmental proceedings.

3. Learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 3-State informs this Court that the inquiry against the petitioner is still pending and in case the petitioner is exonerated in the said inquiry, then NOC as well as gratuity would be released forthwith.

4. In view of the controversy involved in the present case, the present writ petition is disposed of and respondent No.2 is directed to issue necessary instructions to the Inquiry Officer to conclude the departmental inquiry within a period of three months from the date of receiving the certified copy of this order.

5. Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall also stands disposed of. (HARPREET SINGH BRAR) JUDGE August 12, 2025 P.C
